item.title: My data platform diary - Week 1
item.description:
Some of you already know I run a bunch of self-hosted services out of a homelab I’ve been building for over two years now. It started as a place to store personal files, but it’s grown into something a few people in my local community actually rely on.

I work in data engineering for a living, but I’ve never had my own data platform. At some point that stopped making sense to me — I have the infrastructure, I have the knowledge, so why not build one?

item.title: My data platform diary - Week 2
item.description:
Here’s where things stood at the end of last week:

  • MinIO
  • Kafka
  • Stream Nginx logs into a Kafka topic
  • Read the streaming data locally and process it
  • Plan the deploy

Later:

  • Catalog
  • Trino
  • Metabase

Day 1 — Laying out the repo Link to heading

Time to actually start coding. Before writing a single job, I needed to figure out how the repository should be structured — something that could scale in more than one direction without becoming a mess. I also wanted a proper dev environment to test code in before it ever touches the cluster, so I’m setting up a devcontainer with a Spark instance for that.
